texts.preamble: Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.3898/2023 Kabc0B0039232023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath, Llb. Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 29th Day of October 2024 M.V.C. No.3898/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. Chowdappa @ Chavdappa S/o Muniyappa, Aged about 49 years, Residing at: No.2829, 4th Cross, Old Rto, Bhanashankari Layout, Bhattarahalli, Virgonagar, Bangalore-560049. (By Sri. T. Manjunatha, Adv.,) Vs. Respondent/s: 1. The Managing Director, Motor claims Hub, K.S.R.T.C Shanthinagar, Bangalore-560027. [Ksrtc Bus No. Ka-07-F-1740] (By Sri. Adinarayanappa, Adv.,) Date of institution of the : 19.06.2023 petition Scch-21 2 Mvc No.3898/2023 Nature of the Petition : U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act Date of commencement of : 03.07.2024 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 29.10.2024 Chowdappa Alias Chavdappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74446716/ 1 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s 01 04 10 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 17.05.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.05.2023 at about 8.30 p.m., petitioner was standing on the left side of the road, carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules near A2B Hotel, Bhattarahalli O. M. Road, Bangalore, at that time KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-07-F-1740 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, at a high speed and dashed to the petitioner. Due to the forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic Hospital, wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, Conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 49 years, the petitioner doing Coolie work and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent being the owner cum internal insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition as false and contended that the petition is neither maintainable in law nor on facts and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. This respondent further submitted that, the incident was occurred in night at 20.30 hours and the spot of the incident is National Highway road and there is no Zebra crossing at the spot of accident to cross the road by the pedestrian and since the petitioner has tried all of sudden to cross the High way road and came infront of bus, the accident in question has occurred and there is no rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus. Moreover, the petitioner in collusion with certain authorities has filed this false claim petitioner. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and he has examined Dr. Nagaraj. B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.16 and closed their side. On the other hand, the driver of the offending KSRTC bus is examined as RW.1. 6.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 17. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
